english.title: Trader engage in unfair commercial practice by omitting material information from an invitation to purchase
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a trader, engaged in an unfair commercial practice likely to cause the average consumer to take a transactional decision that the consumer would not have taken otherwise as a result of the practice by omitting material from an invitation to purchase, namely **(..SPECIFY MATERIAL..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 237(6) and 240 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a trader
in breach of section 225(1) of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024
engaged in an unfair commercial practice
by omitting material from an invitation to purchase

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 230 on omission of material from invitation to purchase. (ii) Section 238 of the Act provides a defence of due diligence and innocent publication.
(iii) See section 239 for the criminal liability of other persons where the commission of the offence, or what would have been an offence had it not been for a defence, is due to the act or omission of another person (see H101741), and also for corporate liability.
(iv) Section 237(2) makes unfair commercial practice involving a misleading omission an offence, see H101733.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 241
